name: Can luxury materials be installed in older homes with uneven walls and floors?

mainEntity.name: How do installers handle premium stone, tile, and fixtures in older Los Angeles homes that are out of level or out of square?
mainEntity.text: How do installers handle premium stone, tile, and fixtures in older Los Angeles homes that are out of level or out of square?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes can absolutely receive luxury materials, but the installation plan has to account for imperfect structure. Out-of-level floors, bowed walls, and nonstandard framing can throw off slab seams, tile layout, cabinet reveals, and fixture alignment. The installer may need to shim, float, reframe, or rebuild parts of the substrate before finish materials are installed. That prep work is not optional if the goal is a premium result. Luxury materials often have tighter visual tolerances than standard products, so small structural issues become very obvious. Homeowners should ask how the team handles surface correction, what substrate preparation is included, and how much adjustment is possible before the selected materials are affected. In older Los Angeles-area homes, this step often makes the difference between a good-looking room and a truly high-end result.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but the installer usually needs extra prep work to correct framing, level surfaces, and adjust transitions before luxury materials go in. Uneven walls and floors can affect slab alignment, grout lines, fixture placement, and cabinet fit, so proper prep is essential.
